title: Lo, How A Rose E'er Blooming
author: German; Fridrich Layriz (1808-1859)
translator: Theodore Baker (1851-1934); Harriet Reynolds Krauth (1845-1925); Harriet Reynolds Spaeth (1845-1925); John Casper Mattes (1876-1948)
credit: verses 1-2, 15th Century German.  Translated by Theodore Baker, 1894.

tunes.name: Es Ist Ein Ros Entsprungen (Rhythmic)
tunes.composer: Köln, 1599 from Altes Catholische Geistliche Kirchengeseng

firstLine: Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming
verses: Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming
as men of old have sung.
When half spent was the night.
the Rose I have in mind;
she bore to men a Savior,
When half spent was the night.
How Christ, the Lord of glory
was born on earth this night.
and in the manger found Him,
from sin and death He saves us,
Bring us at length we pray,
to the bright courts of Heaven,
